chapters.title: To the Chosen Lady
chapters.html:
2 John 1

1The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not I alone, but also all who have known the truth,

2because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever:

3grace, mercy and peace will be with us, from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

Walking in the Commandment

4I rejoiced greatly to find some of your children walking in truth, just as we received commandment from the Father.

5Now, lady, I ask you, not as though I were writing you a new commandment, but the one we have had from the beginning: that we love one another.

6This is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the commandment, just as you heard from the beginning, that you walk in it.

The Deceiver

7For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess Jesus Christ coming in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the antichrist.

8Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but receive a full reward.

9Everyone who goes too far and does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.

10If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house, and do not give him a greeting;

11for whoever gives him a greeting shares in his evil works.

12Though I have many things to write to you, I did not want to do it with paper and ink; but I hope to come to you and speak face to face, so that your joy may be complete.

13The children of your chosen sister greet you.

Notes

  • v1 "the chosen lady" — eklektē kyria. Kyria is the feminine of kyrios, lord: a lady, a woman of standing. Read as names, the words are Kyria or Eklektē. The letter ends with the children of your chosen sister (v13), which reads most easily as one church greeting another, the lady and her sister as two congregations and their children as their members. The Greek leaves both open, a woman with her household or a church, and so does the chosen lady.

  • v7 "coming in the flesh" — erchomenon en sarki, the present participle. The first letter has the perfect, has come in the flesh (1 John 4:2). The present describes Him as one who comes in the flesh without fixing a time: it can be read of His coming as a man, or of a coming still ahead.

  • v9 "the teaching of Christ" — tē didachē tou Christou can mean the teaching Christ gave or the teaching about Christ; the Greek does not choose.
